subcompetencies.name: Data Acquisition – Basic Ophthalmology Exam and Testing

level_1: Acquires relevant problem-focused history, including outside medical records
Identifies subtle or uncommon examination findings of common disorders and typical or common findings of rarer disorders
level_2: Performs and documents a comprehensive ophthalmic examination; distinguishes between normal and abnormal findings
Interprets unusual findings on routine testing, identifies artifacts; recognizes indications for advanced diagnostic tests and imaging procedures (e.g., specular microscopy, electroretinography)
level_3: Performs problem- focused exam with appropriate techniques (e.g., gonioscopy and scleral depression), consistently identifies common abnormalities on examination; may identify subtle findings
Orders and interprets advanced diagnostic tests and imaging procedures according to evidence-based medicine (i.e., when and when not to order testing)
level_4: Orders, performs, and interprets basic testing (e.g., visual field testing, Optical Coherence
Demonstrates expertise in advanced diagnostic tests and imaging
level_5: Tomography, B-scan)

level_1: Acquires relevant problem-focused history, including outside medical records
Manages consultations (including coordination of care) requiring surgical intervention, including procedural options and timing; requests ophthalmic subspecialty advice, with indirect supervision
level_2: Performs inpatient consultation, with direct supervision
Manages ophthalmic emergencies with non- surgical and surgical treatment, with indirect supervision
level_3: Triages consult requests
Manages consultations (including coordination of care) requiring surgical intervention, including procedural options and timing; requests ophthalmic subspecialty input, with oversight
level_4: Performs a complete examination
Manages ophthalmic emergencies with non- surgical and surgical treatment, with oversight
level_5: Recognizes ophthalmic emergencies and initiates non-surgical treatment plan, with indirect supervision
Oversees the consultation process and manages interdisciplinary systems issues affecting patient care

level_1: Describes essential components of care related to office-based procedures (e.g., informed consent, indications and contraindications, anesthesia, sterile procedure prep)
Administers anesthesia and performs procedure, with oversight
level_2: Administers anesthesia and performs procedure, with direct supervision
Manages intra- and post-operative complications, with oversight
level_3: Recognizes and manages intra- and post-operative complications, with direct supervision
Incorporates recent advancements in technologies or techniques
level_4: Administers anesthesia and performs procedure, with indirect supervision
level_5: Manages intra- and post- operative complications, with indirect supervision

level_1: Identifies visually significant cataract
Assesses patients for complex cataract surgery
Manages complex intra- and post-operative complications (e.g., endophthalmitis)
level_2: Demonstrates ability to scrub, prep and drape patient for surgery; performs basic suturing skills
Performs routine cataract surgery in the OR
Assesses patients for intraocular lenses complications requiring a more complex intervention
level_3: Assesses patients for routine cataract surgery
Manages common intra- and post-operative complications (e.g., posterior capsule rupture, wound leak)
Performs lens surgery for patients with complications requiring a more complex intervention (e.g., sutured intraocular lenses)
level_4: Performs elements of cataract surgery in the hands-on surgical skills laboratory and in the operating room (OR)
Assesses patients who are candidates for refractive intraocular lenses to correct astigmatism and/or provide near correction
Manages rare and complex intra- and post- operative complications (e.g., aqueous misdirection, suprachoroidal hemorrhage)
level_5: Manages common post- operative complications (e.g., post-op pain, high intraocular pressure)
Performs cataract surgery requiring complex technical maneuvers (e.g., pupil expander, capsular tension ring)

level_1: Demonstrates ability to scrub, prep and drape patient for surgery; performs basic suturing skills
Develops a pre-operative plan for routine extraocular surgery
Manages complex intra- and post-operative complications (e.g., infection, retrobulbar hemorrhage)
level_2: Identifies common post- operative complications (e.g., post-op pain, bleeding)
Performs routine extraocular surgery (e.g., complex lid laceration repair, horizontal strabismus, ptosis)
Assess patients and develops a pre-operative plan for complex/ multidisciplinary extraocular surgery (e.g., nerve sheath decompression, vessel sparing strabismus)
level_3: Identifies patients for routine extraocular surgery
Manages intra- and post- operative complications (e.g., bleeding, perforation)
Performs complex extraocular surgery
level_4: Performs simple extraocular surgery (e.g., simple lid laceration repair, nasolacrimal duct probing)
Develops a pre- operative plan for complex extraocular surgery
level_5: Manages common post- operative complications
Performs complex extraocular surgery (e.g., vertical strabismus), with assistance

level_1: Demonstrates ability to scrub, prep and drape patient for surgery; performs basic suturing skills
Assists in subspecialty intraocular surgery
Assess patients requiring surgery from multiple disciplines (e.g., plastic surgery, facial trauma)
level_2: Assesses patients for routine intraocular surgery
Manages common intra- operative complications (e.g., flat chamber, wound leak, hyphema)
Performs complex intraocular surgery
level_3: Performs routine intraocular surgery in the hands-on surgical skills laboratory
Assesses patients for multispecialty intraocular surgeries
Manages rare and complex intra- and post- operative complications (e.g., tube erosion, proliferative vitreoretinopathy)
level_4: Manages common post- operative complications (e.g., post-op pain, high intraocular pressure)
Performs routine intraocular surgery
level_5: Assesses patients for complex intraocular surgery
Manages complex intra- and post-operative complications (e.g., re- bubble graft, blebitis)

level_1: Articulates knowledge of pathophysiology and clinical findings for ophthalmic conditions routinely managed by non-ophthalmologists
level_2: Demonstrates basic knowledge of pathophysiology and clinical findings for common ophthalmic conditions routinely managed by ophthalmologists
level_3: Demonstrates advanced knowledge of pathophysiology and clinical findings for commonly encountered ophthalmic conditions; demonstrates basic knowledge of pathophysiology and clinical findings for uncommon conditions
level_4: Demonstrates advanced knowledge of pathophysiology and clinical findings for uncommon ophthalmic conditions
level_5: Contributes new knowledge for pathophysiology and clinical findings for ophthalmic conditions (e.g., publication, curriculum development)

level_1: Identifies resources to generate a focused differential
Selects additional diagnostic testing to distinguish between conditions on the differential
level_2: Generates a basic differential diagnosis based on patient symptoms and history
Generates probabilistic differential diagnosis in patients with multiple ocular and medical comorbidities; modifies likely differential with new information from additional testing
level_3: Generates comprehensive differential diagnosis based on patient symptoms and history; documents and presents differential in oral presentation clearly and concisely
Articulates the rationale for ordering diagnostic testing in hierarchical fashion based upon probabilistic differential
level_4: Describes diagnostic tests to aid in the differential diagnosis
Recognizes, self-reflects, and shares experiences to educate others on factors that contributed to missed diagnosis or faulty clinical reasoning (e.g., publication, curriculum development)
level_5: Generates refined differential based on patient symptoms, history and examination findings, distinguishing between common and uncommon conditions

level_1: Describes basic concepts of ophthalmic pathophysiology and pharmacology
Identifies and describes causes of complications and alternatives for routine procedural interventions
level_2: Describes basic ophthalmic anatomy and categories of procedural interventions
Describes and articulates the rationale for using emerging alternative medical therapies
level_3: Explains relevant pathophysiology and lists indications and contraindications for planned medical therapy
Describes and articulates the rationale for using novel alternative procedural interventions
level_4: Explains indications, contraindications, and relevant steps required for procedural intervention (e.g., anesthesia, technique, instruments)
Participates in the development and dissemination of novel therapies or interventions
level_5: Identifies and describes side effects of medical therapies and ways to minimize potential complications

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of common patient safety events
Describes local quality improvement initiatives (e.g., eye protection for high risk activities, diabetic eye screening)
Discloses patient safety events to patients and families (simulated or actual)
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of how to report patient safety events
Participates in analysis of patient safety events (simulated or actual)
Demonstrates the skills required to identify, develop, implement, and analyze a quality improvement project
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of basic quality improvement methodologies and metrics
Participates in disclosure of patient safety events to patients and families (simulated or actual)
Actively engages teams and processes to modify systems to prevent patient safety events
level_4: Identifies system factors that lead to patient safety events
Participates in local quality improvement initiatives
Role models or mentors others in the disclosure of patient safety events
level_5: Reports patient safety events through institutional reporting systems (simulated or actual)
Conducts analysis of patient safety events and offers error prevention strategies (simulated or actual)
Creates, implements, and assesses quality improvement initiatives at the institutional or community level

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of care coordination
Demonstrates knowledge of local population and community health needs for their local population
Advocates for safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs within and across health care delivery systems
level_2: Identifies key elements for safe and effective transitions of care and hand-offs
Coordinates care of patients in complex clinical situations effectively using the roles of their interprofessional teams
Uses local resources effectively to meet the needs of a patient population and community
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of the role of the physician in addressing community health needs
Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in complex clinical situations
Analyzes the process of care coordination and leads in the design and implementation of improvements
level_4: Coordinates care of patients in routine clinical situations effectively using the roles of the interprofessional teams
Identifies specific local health needs related to ophthalmic care
Improves quality of transitions of care within and across health care delivery systems to optimize patient outcomes
level_5: Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in routine clinical situations
Teaches effective coordination of patient- centered care among different disciplines and specialties to junior members of the team
Participates in changing and adapting practice to provide for the needs of specific populations

subcompetencies.name: Physician Role in Health Care Systems

level_1: Describes basic health care systems and access models (e.g., government, private, public, uninsured care)
Describes knowledge domains for effective transition to practice (e.g., information technology, legal, billing and coding)
level_2: Demonstrates use of electronic medical record
Advocates for patient care needs beyond patients’ available resources (e.g., community resources, patient assistance resources, telehealth)
level_3: Describes how different system types require the physician to deliver care effectively with available resources
Demonstrates administrative knowledge needed for transition to practice (e.g., contract negotiations, malpractice insurance, government regulation, compliance)
level_4: Identifies the documentation required for billing and coding compliance
Participates in health policy advocacy activities
level_5: Optimizes patient care given available resources
Analyzes individual practice patterns and professional requirements in preparation for practice

level_1: Demonstrates how to access and use available evidence, and incorporate patient preferences and values in order to take care of a routine patient
level_2: Articulates clinical questions and elicits patient preferences and values in order to guide evidence-based care
level_3: Locates and applies the best available evidence, integrated with patient preference, to the care of complex patients
level_4: Critically appraises and applies evidence even in the face of uncertainty and conflicting evidence to guide care, tailored to the individual patient
level_5: Coaches others to critically appraise and apply evidence for complex patients; and/or participates in the development of patient care guidelines

subcompetencies.name: Reflective Practice and Commitment to Personal Growth

level_1: Accepts responsibility for personal and professional development by establishing goals; actively seeks opportunities to improve
Analyzes, reflects on, and institutes behavioral change(s) to narrow the gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
level_2: Identifies the factors which contribute to gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
Uses performance data to measure the effectiveness of the learning plan and when necessary, improves it
level_3: Demonstrates openness to performance data (feedback and other input) in order to inform goals; designs and implements a learning plan, with guidance
Challenges assumptions and considers alternatives in narrowing the gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
level_4: Analyzes and reflects on the factors which contribute to gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
Facilitates the design and implementing learning plans for others
level_5: Seeks performance data and accepts it with responsibility and equipoise; demonstrates implementation of a learning plan
Coaches others on reflective practice

level_1: Identifies and describes potential triggers for professionalism lapses
Analyzes straightforward situations using ethical principles
Recognizes and uses appropriate resources for managing and resolving ethical dilemmas as needed (e.g., ethics consultations, literature review, risk management/legal consultation)
level_2: Describes when and how to appropriately report professionalism lapses, including strategies for addressing common barriers
Demonstrates professional behavior in complex or stressful situations
Coaches others when their behavior fails to meet professional expectations
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of the ethical principles underlying informed consent, surrogate decision making, advance directives, confidentiality, error disclosure, stewardship of limited resources, and related topics
Recognizes need to seek help in managing and resolving complex ethical situations
Identifies and seeks to address system-level factors that induce or exacerbate ethical problems or impede their resolution
level_4: Demonstrates insight into professional behavior in routine situations
Analyzes complex situations using ethical principles
level_5: Takes responsibility for own professionalism lapses
Recognizes situations that may trigger professionalism lapses and intervenes to prevent lapses in self and others

level_1: Takes responsibility for failure to complete tasks and responsibilities, identifies potential contributing factors, and describes strategies for ensuring timely task completion in the future
Recognizes detrimental consequences when tasks and responsibilities are not completed in a timely manner (e.g., team members, compliance)
level_2: Responds promptly to requests or reminders to complete tasks and responsibilities
Recognizes situations that may impact others’ ability to complete tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner
level_3: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with attention to detail in routine situations
Proactively implements strategies to ensure that the needs of patients, teams, and systems are met
level_4: Recognizes situations that may impact own ability to complete tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner
Takes ownership of system outcomes, attempts to implement changes at a systems level in order to advance the goals of professional accountability
level_5: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with attention to detail in complex or stressful situations

level_1: Recognizes status of personal and professional well-being, with assistance
With assistance, proposes a plan to improve knowledge/skills of self and/or team
level_2: Recognizes limits in the knowledge/skills of self and/or team, with assistance
Independently develops a plan to optimize personal and professional well-being
level_3: Independently recognizes status of personal and professional well-being
Independently develops a plan to improve the knowledge/skills of self and/or team
level_4: Independently recognizes limits in the knowledge/ skills of self and/or team; demonstrates appropriate help-seeking behaviors for self or others
Coaches others when emotional responses or limitations in knowledge/skills do not meet professional expectations
level_5: With assistance, proposes a plan to optimize personal and professional well-being

level_1: Uses language and nonverbal behavior to demonstrate respect and establish rapport
When prompted, reflects on biases while attempting to minimize communication barriers
level_2: Identifies barriers to effective communication (e.g., health literacy, language, disability) while accurately communicating own role within the health care system
Easily establishes therapeutic relationships, with attention to patient/family concerns and context, regardless of complexity
level_3: Establishes a therapeutic relationship in straightforward encounters using active listening and clear language
Role models self- awareness to minimize communication barriers
level_4: Addresses barriers to effective communication
Mentors others in situational awareness and critical self-reflection to consistently develop positive therapeutic relationships
level_5: Establishes a therapeutic relationship in challenging patient encounters (e.g., breaking bad news)

level_1: Uses language that values all members of the health care team
Provides feedback and constructive criticism to peers and learners
level_2: Accepts feedback on performance from all members of the health care team (e.g., nurses, staff members, peers)
Role models flexible communication strategies that value input from all health care team members, resolving conflict when needed
level_3: Communicates information effectively and uses active listening with all health care team members
Provides feedback and constructive criticism to superiors
level_4: Solicits feedback on performance as a member of the health care team
Facilitates regular health care team-based feedback in complex situations
level_5: Communicates concerns to the team and learners

level_1: Accurately records information in the medical record
Identifies appropriate channels to communicate system deficiencies
Provides feedback and constructive criticism regarding compliance with patient privacy and safety
level_2: Aware of the role of communication in patient safety and privacy; safeguards patient personal health information
Communicates clearly and concisely, including anticipatory guidance, in the medical record
Offers clear and constructive suggestions to address system deficiencies
level_3: Aware of responsibility to report system deficiencies
Avoids creating or propagating errors in the medical record through accurate use of documentation tools
Facilitates dialogue regarding systems issues among larger community stakeholders (institution, health care system, field)
level_4: Demonstrates organized diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning through notes in the medical record
Uses appropriate channels to communicate system deficiencies
Guides departmental or institutional communication around policies and procedures
level_5: Appropriately selects forms of communication (e.g., telephone versus text) to promote patient safety and privacy
Provides feedback to improve others’ written communication
